items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: Uncle Coleman had built many of the houses as he was a Jack of all trades... He built the school and his own house which was the largest in the village.

ctx.x: I must have been 4 years old when I started to realise certain things. CENTERVILLE was a village with a population of 450 people, one Baptist Church, one Episcopalian Church, one barbor shop for men, a general store that sold clothing, farm ware and was also the post office, and had the only public telephone in the village.

The population was mostly negro, but the general store, the blacksmith shop, and the thrasher machine were owned by white people, and the village doctor for everybody was white. The village was beautiful because some part of it was on a hill and the houses were all built of wood except the Baptist Church, which was built with bricks. Uncle Coleman had built many of the houses as he was a Jack of all trades, and good at all of them. He built the school and his own house which was the largest in the village.

I also remember that my grand-mother Coleman lived in a 4-room log cabin. Any house built of logs was a cabin and this was the only one in Centerville. I never knew if it was Uncle John that built it.
